To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the resistance of lactococci to hydrolysis by lysozyme depends on the degree of acetylation of the peptidogycan and is regulated by a two-component system, CesSR, that responds to the stress caused by the hydrolysis of the cell wall.

the resistance of Gram-positive non-pathogenic bacterium Lactococcus to lysozyme hydrolysis is dependent on the degree of acetylation of PG achieved by the over-expression of deacetylase (PgdA) or O acetylase (OatA), the latter being regulated by SpxB, a regulator of the two-component system (CesSR), which in turn responds to the envelope stress.

i) Lactococcus spp. are able to respond to stress by activating a two-component regulatory system, which is involved in the regulation of the expression of several genes, such as spxB, oatA, and pdgA, and that ii) the expression of oatA, spxB, and pdg, which are involved in the regulation and synthesis of PG, are involved in the stress response of Lactococcus to lysozyme and to antibiotics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the cell wall in the response of L. lactis to environmental stress.
understanding the molecular mechanisms involved in the response of the cell wall to the damage induced by the autolysins.
the response of lactococci to damage of their peptidogylcan (PG) envelope.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PG is a complex and dynamic structure, which is constantly remodelling in order to adapt to the changing environment of the bacterial cell.

the PG of L. lactis is a complex macromolecule that is subjected to several modifications by PG modifying enzymes and that these modifications have an important impact on the cell wall architecture, cell wall stability, cell physiology and stress resistance.
the genes responsible for the stress response to the PG damage, are responsible for the resistance to the lysozyme and the resistance to the antibiotics aminoglycose and vancomycin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the stress response to envelope damage is a complex process involving a number of proteins that act as regulators of the stress response.

the PG is a dynamic and complex structure that can be modified in response to various stresses and that these modifications can affect the resistance of the bacterium to the hydrolytic enzymes and to antibiotics.

we demonstrated that the stress response of L. lactis to the damage of PG is controlled by a complex regulatory network that includes a two-component regulatory system, a transcriptional regulator, a PG hydrolase, and a deacetylase.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the response of Lactococcus to the stress of PG damage is not limited to the genes involved in PG synthesis, but also includes genes involved in the stress response.
the genes involved in the stress response to envelope damage are also responsible for the antibiotic resistance of L. lactis.

the PG of L. lactis is a dynamic molecule, which can be modified by different enzymes, such as deacetylases and O acetylases, and that these modifications have a major impact on the PG structure and consequently on the resistance of L. lactiss to PG hydrolyzing enzymes, such as lysozyme.
